MeetGeek has a free plan, with paid tiers starting at **$9.99 per user/month when billed annually**. Month-to-month prices are higher: Pro is $15.99/user/month and Business is $27/user/month.[1]

## MeetGeek pricing

| Plan | Price | Core limits / inclusions |
|---|---:|---|
| Free | $0 | 3 transcription hours per month, 3 months of transcript storage, and 1 month of audio storage. [1] |
| Pro | $15.99/user/month monthly, or $9.99/user/month annually | 20 transcription hours/month, 1 year of transcript storage, 6 months of audio storage; extra transcription costs $0.50/hour. [1] |
| Business | $27/user/month monthly, or $17/user/month annually | Unlimited transcription and transcript storage, plus 12 months of video storage. [1] |
| Enterprise | Custom quote | Unlimited transcription and transcript storage, with customizable video-storage terms and organization-level controls. [1] |

## Billing note

The advertised lower prices—$9.99 for Pro and $17 for Business—are the **annual-billing** rates. MeetGeek says annual payment can save up to 40%, so compare the annual commitment with your expected meeting volume before choosing it.[1]

## Which tier fits

- Choose **Free** for occasional meetings or to test the transcription and summary workflow.
- Choose **Pro** if you regularly record meetings but stay near or below 20 hours monthly; above that, factor in the $0.50/hour overage.[1]
- Choose **Business** for teams or anyone with heavy meeting volume, since its unlimited transcription can become cheaper and simpler than recurring Pro overages.[1]
- Choose **Enterprise** if you need a tailored contract, storage policy, or company-wide deployment controls.[1]

TextExpander has a **free plan**, plus paid Pro, Business, and custom Enterprise tiers. The published U.S. annual-billing prices are **$5/user/month for Pro** ($60/year) and **$10/user/month for Business** ($120/year); its pricing page also displays $6 and $12 per user/month figures, likely reflecting the selected billing/local-tax presentation, so verify the checkout total for your location.[1]

## Plans at a glance

| Plan | Price | Best for | Main limits/features |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Free | $0 | Trying it personally or light use | 5 active snippets, one “Snippet Swap” every two weeks, and sharing with up to 5 members across 3 teams |
| Pro | $5/user/month billed annually ($60/year) | Individual power users | Unlimited expansions and broader paid features |
| Business | $10/user/month billed annually ($120/year) | Teams needing shared, standardized text | Shared snippet libraries and collaboration |
| Enterprise | Custom | Organizations with security/admin needs | Business features plus advanced security and administration |

TextExpander says monthly billing is available, while annual billing effectively gives two months free. New accounts receive a **30-day preview of paid features**, and the Free plan does not require a credit card.[1]

## Important pricing details

- Prices are in USD, per user, and tax may be added or built into displayed pricing depending on country—particularly for VAT/GST jurisdictions.[1]
- Enterprise is quote-based, so you would need to contact TextExpander for final pricing.[1]
- For a small team of five on annual Business, the listed base cost would be \(5 \times \$120 = \$600\) per year, before any applicable taxes.[1]

WhatConverts’ public pricing starts at **$30/month** for a single account, with higher tiers at $60, $100, and $160 per month. Plans also include a monthly usage credit; tracking activity beyond that credit can add charges.[1][2]

## Plans

| Plan | Starting price | Main coverage |
|---|---:|---|
| Call Tracking | $30/month | Phone-call and text-message tracking |
| Plus | $60/month | Calls, forms, and chat tracking; campaign/keyword reporting and ad/analytics integrations |
| Pro | $100/month | Adds call flows/routing, report builder, scheduled reports, and HIPAA-oriented features |
| Elite | $160/month | Highest listed standard tier; check the live plan page for the exact feature set |

The reported standard plans include a **$30 monthly usage credit**.[2]

## How usage charges work

Your bill is generally:

\[
\text{monthly plan fee} + \text{usage above included credit} + \text{optional add-ons}
\]

Usage can include:

- Tracking phone numbers, which carry a recurring number fee
- Call minutes, varying by country and local versus toll-free numbers
- Form and chat leads, charged per tracked submission
- Optional call transcription, billed by audio minute
- PCI redaction and potentially extended recording storage or white-label features[3]

## Free trial and estimate

WhatConverts advertises a **14-day free trial**. Its pricing page also includes a calculator where you can enter expected call, form, and chat volume to estimate the monthly total and find the appropriate plan.[1][4]

For the current exact price in your country and projected usage cost, use the official [WhatConverts pricing page](https://www.whatconverts.com/pricing/), since phone-number and call-forwarding rates can vary by location and configuration.

Replit currently offers a free Starter tier plus paid Core, Pro, and Enterprise plans. The main variable beyond the subscription price is usage: AI Agent work, hosting/deployments, and compute draw from included credits, then may incur pay-as-you-go charges.[1][2]

## Plan prices

| Plan | Monthly price | Annual-billing price | Included monthly credits | Best suited to |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Starter | Free | Free | Free daily Agent credits | Trying Replit and small personal experiments |
| Core | $25/month | $20/month | $25 | Personal projects and simple apps |
| Pro | $100/month | $95/month | $100 | Professional/commercial projects and small teams |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom | Custom | Organizations needing enterprise controls |

Prices can be subject to local taxes. Replit advertises annual savings of up to 20%.[1]

## What each tier includes

- **Starter:** Free daily Agent credits, a built-in database for full-stack apps, tools to create slides/videos/animations, and publication of up to one project, including private or password-protected deployments.[1]
- **Core:** Everything in Starter, $25 in monthly credits, up to five collaborators, and up to two parallel Agent tasks. Replit’s documentation also describes full Agent Plan and Build modes, unlimited published apps, and a seven-day database restore window.[1][2]
- **Pro:** Everything in Core, $100 monthly credits, up to 15 collaborators/builders, greater Agent capacity, priority support, and a 28-day database restore window. Unused Pro credits can roll over for a limited period.[2][3]
- **Enterprise:** Adds capabilities such as custom seat limits, SSO/SAML, and advanced privacy controls.[1]

## Hosting and overages

Your plan’s included credits are applied to publishing/deployment costs first. When those credits are depleted, applicable usage charges can continue on a pay-as-you-go basis.[4]

Common starting points cited by Replit:

- Autoscale deployments: from $1/month on Core, plus usage that scales with demand
- Scheduled deployments: from $1/month on Core
- Reserved VM deployments: from $20/month on Core
- Static deployments: no server-compute charge; data transfer can still apply. Core includes 100 GiB/month, and Starter includes one free static deployment.[5]

## Practical choice

- Choose **Starter** if you are learning, prototyping, or want to test the Agent without a subscription.
- Choose **Core** if you want recurring AI credits, more publishing flexibility, and a small collaboration setup.
- Choose **Pro** if you are building client-facing or commercial apps, need more concurrent Agent work, or work with a team of up to 15.
- Pick **Enterprise** only if your organization needs centralized controls such as SSO and specialized privacy/security terms.

One important caveat: credits power both AI and infrastructure-related activity, so a plan’s sticker price is not necessarily your total cost. Set usage/spend controls and monitor the credit balance if you plan to run an always-on app or use the Agent heavily.[2][4]

Todoist has a free plan, plus paid Pro and Business plans. Current listed pricing is **$7/month or $60/year for Pro**, and **$10 per user/month or $96 per user/year for Business**, before any applicable local tax.[1]

## Plans at a glance

| Plan | Price | Best for | Key limits/features |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Beginner | Free | Basic personal task management | 5 personal projects, 3 filters, 5 MB uploads, one week of activity history |
| Pro | $7/month, or $60/year | Individuals with many projects or advanced planning needs | 300 personal projects, calendar layout, task duration, custom reminders, 150 filters, full reporting history, deadlines |
| Business | $10/user/month, or $8/user/month billed annually ($96/user/year) | Teams | Everything in Pro, plus shared workspace, up to 500 team projects, team folders, roles/permissions, centralized billing, and activity logs |

The annual billing equivalents work out to **$5/month for Pro** and **$8/user/month for Business**.[1]

## Which one to choose

- Choose **Beginner** if you just need a personal to-do list and can work within five projects.
- Choose **Pro** if you want robust recurring planning, many projects, custom reminders, calendar planning, and long-term task history.
- Choose **Business** if you need organization-wide collaboration controls, a shared team workspace, team project organization, and centralized billing.

Todoist says Pro has no separate student, family, or nonprofit discount; paying annually is the stated lower-cost option versus monthly Pro billing.[2]

Beehiiv has a free tier for up to 2,500 subscribers, while paid plans are priced by active-subscriber tier rather than email volume. Every plan includes unlimited sends; Beehiiv also says it takes **0%** of paid-subscription revenue, excluding Stripe’s processing fees.[1]

## Current plan overview

| Plan | Starting price | Subscriber limit | Best for |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Launch | $0/month | Up to 2,500 | New or small newsletters |
| Scale | $43/month when billed annually | Pricing scales up to 100,000 subscribers | Monetization, automations, growth tools |
| Max | $96/month when billed annually | Pricing scales up to 100,000 subscribers | Larger teams and white-label/advanced publishing needs |
| Enterprise | Custom | 100,000+ or custom needs | High-volume organizations |

The listed annual-billing starting totals are $517/year for Scale and $1,151/year for Max.[1]

## Monthly vs. annual pricing

At the entry subscriber tier, Scale is listed around **$49/month** on monthly billing or $43/month equivalent on annual billing; Max is about **$109/month** monthly or $96/month equivalent annually. Prices rise at subscriber thresholds, so the figure shown during checkout depends on the count of active subscribers in your publication.[2][3]

Examples of monthly pricing reported for paid plans:

| Active subscribers | Scale | Max |
|---:|---:|---:|
| Up to 1,000 | $49/month | $109/month |
| Up to 2,500 | $69/month | $149/month |
| Up to 5,000 | $89/month | $169/month |
| Up to 10,000 | $109/month | $219/month |
| Up to 25,000 | $169/month | $289/month |
| Up to 100,000 | $329/month | $459/month |

These are monthly-billing figures; annual payment reduces the effective monthly rate.[2][4]

## What the plans mean

- **Launch:** A no-cost starting option with up to 2,500 subscribers and unlimited email sends. It is suitable for testing a newsletter before paying for growth or monetization features.[1]
- **Scale:** The core creator/business plan. It adds monetization capabilities and tools such as automations and A/B testing.[2][4]
- **Max:** Adds more advanced publishing and team capabilities, including removal of Beehiiv branding, more publications, and expanded support/team features.[4][5]
- **Enterprise:** Custom pricing for lists above 100,000 subscribers or organizations requiring tailored limits and support.[1][3]

## Revenue fees

For paid subscriptions, Beehiiv says its platform fee is 0%, so you retain subscription revenue apart from Stripe’s stated standard transaction processing charge of 2.9% plus $0.30 per transaction. That can matter more than the monthly software price if your newsletter has meaningful paid-subscription revenue.[1]

For the exact current cost for your list size—especially if you are near a tier boundary—use Beehiiv’s [pricing calculator](https://www.beehiiv.com/pricing), since paid-plan pricing changes with active subscriber count.[3]

Airwallex pricing varies by the country where your business entity is registered and by what you use—accounts, FX conversion, transfers, cards, or payment acceptance. In the US, its entry-level **Explore** plan is listed at $0; **Grow** is $12 per user per month plus a team-size-based platform fee.[1]

## US plan pricing

| Plan | Published monthly price | Intended use |
|---|---:|---|
| Explore | $0 | Core global accounts, transfers, and business spending |
| Grow | $12 per user/month, plus platform fee | More advanced financial and spend-management controls |
| Enterprise/API/embedded finance | Custom quote | Higher-volume or platform/embedded-finance needs |

Airwallex states that subscription charges apply per business legal entity, not per individual account. Transaction charges can still apply on top of the subscription for services such as currency exchange, transfers, and card-payment processing.[1]

## Important transaction costs

Common costs to check before choosing Airwallex include:

- **FX conversion:** commonly quoted as a 0.5% markup above the interbank rate for selected major currencies, and 1.0% for other currencies; exact availability and rates depend on the market and product.[2]
- **Card payment acceptance in the US:** third-party pricing summaries report 2.8% + $0.30 for domestic cards and 4.3% + $0.30 for international cards; confirm the current rate in Airwallex’s fee schedule before relying on it.[2]
- **SWIFT transfers:** third-party summaries cite $15 for shared-fee transfers and $25 where the sender covers charges, potentially excluding intermediary-bank deductions.[2]
- **Corporate cards:** cards are generally described as having no annual fee or issuance fee, though plan limits, user costs, and eligibility can apply.[2]

## Outside the US

Pricing is materially different by region. For example, Airwallex’s UK pricing has been published as:

- Explore: £0 if the business deposits or holds at least £10,000; otherwise £19/month
- Grow: £49/month
- Accelerate: from £999/month
- Enterprise: custom pricing[3]

## What this means in practice

For a small US business that only needs multicurrency accounts and occasional transfers, the $0 Explore plan may be sufficient—but FX and transfer charges may become the main cost. If staff need expense controls and frequent company-card use, Grow’s per-user and platform pricing can matter more than the headline $12 rate.

Use Airwallex’s country-specific pricing page and detailed fee schedule for the legal entity’s registration country, since the plan fee, free-tier conditions, and payment-processing rates can differ substantially by location.[1]
